verses.text: The proverbs of Solomon, David's son and king of Israel.
They're here so you can learn wisdom and instruction and recognize words that give insight.
They teach you how to act wisely and do what's right, just, and fair.
They give good judgment to the inexperienced, and knowledge and discretion to young people.
Let wise people listen and learn even more. Let people with understanding get sound advice.
Learn to understand proverbs and parables, the sayings and riddles of the wise.
Reverence for the LORD is where knowledge begins. Fools look down on wisdom and instruction.
My son, listen to what your father teaches you. Don't walk away from your mother's instruction.
Their teaching is like a crown of flowers on your head and a chain of honor around your neck.
My son, if people pull you toward sin, don't go along.
They might say, “Come with us. Let's wait in hiding to spill blood. Let's ambush innocent people for no reason.
Let's swallow them alive like Sheol, whole like people going down to the pit.
We'll get all kinds of valuables and fill our homes with stolen goods.
Join our crew. We'll all share the same purse.”
My son, don't go down that road with them. Keep your feet off their path.
Their feet run toward evil. They're in a hurry to spill blood.
There's no point spreading a net where a bird can see it.
But these people are setting an ambush for themselves. They're putting their own lives in the trap.
That's where greed for profit leads. It takes the lives of the people who chase it.
Wisdom calls out in the street. She raises her voice in the public squares.
She calls out over the noise. At the entrance to the city gates, here's what she says:
“How long will you who lack judgment be happy to stay that way? How long will mockers love mocking and fools hate knowledge?
Turn around when I correct you. Look, I'll pour out my spirit on you and make my words known to you.
I called, and you refused to listen. I reached out my hand, and nobody paid attention.
You brushed off all my advice and wanted nothing to do with my correction.
So I'll laugh when disaster hits you. I'll mock when trouble catches up with you,
when calamity sweeps in like a storm and disaster hits like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish close in.
Then they'll call out to me, but I won't answer. They'll look hard for me, but they won't find me,
because they hated knowledge and never chose to revere the LORD.
They wanted nothing to do with my advice and despised every correction I gave.
So they'll eat the fruit of their choices and get their fill of their own schemes.
The inexperienced will die because they turned away, and fools will be destroyed by their own carelessness.
But whoever listens to me will live safely and be at ease, without fear of harm.”
My son, take in my words and store my commands inside you.
Tune your ear to wisdom and give your whole heart to understanding.
Call out for good judgment. Raise your voice for understanding.
Look for wisdom like you'd look for silver. Search for it like buried treasure.
Then you'll understand what it means to revere the LORD and come to know God.
The LORD gives wisdom. Knowledge and understanding come straight from him.
He stores up sound wisdom for people who live uprightly. He's a shield for those who walk with integrity,
guarding the paths of justice and keeping his faithful people safe on their way.
Then you'll understand what's right, just, and fair, and recognize every good path.
Wisdom will make its home in your heart. Knowledge will be a joy to your soul.
Good judgment will watch over you, and understanding will keep you safe.
They'll rescue you from the road to evil and from people whose words twist what's right,
people who leave the straight paths to walk in darkness,
who celebrate doing evil and get a kick out of its crooked ways,
whose roads are crooked and whose paths lead them astray.
Wisdom will rescue you from the strange woman, the outsider who draws you in with flattery.
She walks away from the partner of her youth and forgets the covenant she made before God.
Her house leads down to death. Her paths lead to the spirits of the dead.
None who go to her come back or find their way to the paths of life.
So walk with people who do good and stay on the paths of those who do what's right.
The upright will live in the land. People of integrity will remain there.
But the wicked will be cut off from the land. Those who betray others will be pulled up by the roots.
My son, remember what I've taught you. Keep my commands in your heart.
They'll give you more days, years of life, and peace.
Hold on to kindness and truth. Tie them around your neck and write them on the tablet of your heart.
Then you'll find favor and be known for good judgment before God and people.
Trust the LORD with your whole heart. Don't lean on your own understanding.
Recognize him in everything you do, and he'll straighten your paths.
Don't act wise in your own eyes. Revere the LORD and turn away from evil.
That will bring health to your body and strength to your bones.
Honor the LORD with what you have and with the first fruits of everything you gain.
Then your barns will be full and your vats will overflow with new wine.
My son, don't look down on the LORD's discipline or get tired of his correction.
The LORD corrects the people he loves, like a father correcting the son he delights in.
Happy is anyone who finds wisdom and gains understanding.
What wisdom brings is worth more than silver. What she gives back is better than pure gold.
She's more precious than rubies. Nothing you could want compares to her.
She holds long life in her right hand and riches and honor in her left.
Her ways are pleasant, and all her paths lead in peace.
She's a tree of life to those who take hold of her. Happy is everyone who holds on. 🌳
By wisdom the LORD laid the earth's foundations. By understanding he set the heavens in place.
By his knowledge the depths broke open and the skies dropped down dew.
My son, keep sound wisdom and good judgment in sight. Don't let them go.
They'll bring life to your soul and grace to your neck.
Then you'll walk safely on your way. Your feet won't stumble.
When you lie down, you won't be afraid. You'll lie down and sleep well.
Don't be afraid when terror comes out of nowhere or when destruction comes on the wicked.
The LORD will be the one you trust, and he'll keep your foot from getting caught.
When you have the power to do good for someone who deserves it, don't hold back.
Don't tell your neighbor, “Go away and come back tomorrow. I'll give it to you then,” when you already have it with you.
Don't plot harm against your neighbor when they're living beside you in trust.
Don't pick a fight with someone for no reason when they've done you no harm.
Don't envy violent people or take up any of their ways.
The LORD detests people who twist what's right, but he's a friend to those who live uprightly.
The LORD's curse is on the home of the wicked. He blesses the home of those who do right.
He mocks the mockers and gives grace to the humble.
Wise people will inherit honor. Fools will get nothing but shame for their trouble.
Listen, sons, to a father's instruction. Pay attention so you can learn understanding.
I'm giving you sound teaching. Don't walk away from what I teach you.
I was my father's son once, still young and the only child in my mother's eyes.
My father taught me and said, “Hold my words in your heart. Keep my commands and live.
Get wisdom. Get understanding. Don't forget what I say or turn aside from my words.
Don't abandon wisdom, and she'll protect you. Love her and she'll keep you safe.
Wisdom comes first. Get wisdom, and even if it costs everything you own, get understanding.
Value her and she'll lift you up. Hold her close and she'll bring you honor.
She'll place a garland of grace on your head and give you a crown of splendor.”
Listen, my son, and take my words to heart. You'll have many years to live.
I've taught you the way of wisdom. I've led you along straight paths.
When you walk, nothing will hold back your steps. When you run, you won't trip.
Hold on tight to instruction. Don't let her go. Guard her, because she's your life.
Stay off the path of the wicked. Don't walk the road that evil people take.
Avoid it completely. Turn away and keep going.
They can't sleep unless they've done something wrong. They're wide awake until they make someone fall.
Wickedness is their bread, and violence is their wine.
The path of those who do what's right is like dawn, getting brighter until the day is in full light. 🌅
The road of the wicked is pitch dark. They don't even know what trips them up.
My son, pay attention to what I say. Listen closely to my words.
Keep them in sight. Hold them right at the center of your heart.
They're life to everyone who finds them and health for their whole body.
Guard your heart with all you've got. It's where life flows from.
Get crooked talk out of your mouth. Keep dishonest words far from your lips.
Look straight ahead. Keep your eyes on what's right in front of you.
Make the path under your feet level and keep every step steady.
Don't veer right or left. Keep your feet away from evil.
My son, pay attention to my wisdom. Listen closely to what I've learned,
so you can keep your good judgment and speak from knowledge.
An adulteress can make her words drip like honey. Her talk is smoother than oil,
but in the end she's as bitter as wormwood and as sharp as a double-edged sword.
Her feet go down to death. Her steps take her straight to Sheol.
She gives no thought to the path of life. Her ways are crooked, and she doesn't even know it.
Now listen, my sons. Don't turn away from what I'm telling you.
Stay far from her. Don't even go near her door,
or you'll hand your honor to other people and give your years to someone cruel.
Strangers will live off your wealth, and all your hard work will make someone else's household rich.
At the end of it all, when your body is worn away, you'll groan
and say, “I hated being taught. Deep down I couldn't stand being corrected.
I ignored my teachers and didn't listen to anyone who tried to teach me.
I've come this close to total ruin, with the whole community watching.”
Drink water from your own cistern, fresh water from your own well.
Should your springs spill out in the streets, your streams run through public squares?
Let them be yours alone. Keep them from strangers.
May your spring be blessed. Find joy in the wife of your youth.
She's like a loving doe, a graceful deer. Let her breasts satisfy you always. Stay captivated by her love.
My son, why get caught up with an adulteress? Why hold another woman close?
The LORD sees the way everyone lives. He examines every path they take.
The wicked get caught in their own wrongdoing. Their sin holds them tight like ropes.
They'll die for lack of instruction. Their own deep foolishness will lead them astray.
My son, if you've guaranteed a debt for your neighbor or shaken hands on a pledge for a stranger,
your own words have caught you. What you said has put you in a trap.
Here's how to get free, my son, now that you're at your neighbor's mercy. Go humble yourself and plead with your neighbor. Don't let it drop.
Don't let yourself sleep or even close your eyes for a nap.
Get free like a gazelle escaping a hunter or a bird getting out of a trap.
Go watch the ant, you slacker. Pay attention to how she lives and learn some wisdom. 🐜
She has no boss, supervisor, or ruler,
yet she stores up food in summer and gathers her supplies at harvest.
How long will you sleep, slacker? When are you getting up?
A little more sleep, a little more dozing, a little folding of your hands to rest,
and poverty will come at you like a robber, and need like an armed man.
A worthless person who does wrong goes around talking crooked,
winking, giving signals with their feet, and making signs with their fingers.
Their heart is twisted. They're always plotting harm and stirring up conflict.
So disaster will hit them without warning. They'll break down suddenly, and there'll be no fixing it.
There are six things the LORD hates, seven he finds detestable:
arrogant eyes, a lying tongue, hands that spill innocent blood,
a heart that cooks up wicked schemes, feet that run straight to trouble,
a false witness who tells lies, and anyone who stirs up fights between brothers.
My son, keep your father's command and hold on to your mother's teaching.
Tie them to your heart for good. Fasten them around your neck.
Their teaching will guide you when you walk, watch over you when you sleep, and speak to you when you wake up.
A command is a lamp and teaching is a light. Correction that teaches you opens the way to life,
keeping you from the immoral woman and the smooth talk of an unfaithful wife.
Don't let her beauty stir up lust in your heart or let her looks pull you in.
A prostitute can leave you with nothing but a piece of bread. An adulteress is hunting for your precious life.
Can you scoop fire into your lap without burning your clothes?
Can you walk on hot coals without scorching your feet?
That's what it's like to sleep with your neighbor's wife. Whoever touches her won't get away without punishment.
People don't despise a thief who steals because they're hungry,
but if they're caught, they must pay back seven times what they took, even if it costs everything in their house.
Anyone who commits adultery lacks understanding. They're destroying their own life.
They'll end up wounded and disgraced. Their shame won't be wiped away.
Jealousy makes the husband furious. When he takes revenge, he won't hold back.
He won't take payment to settle it or be satisfied, no matter how many gifts you offer.
My son, hold on to my words. Store my commands inside you.
Keep my commands and live! Protect what I teach you like the pupil of your eye.
Tie these words around your fingers. Write them on the tablet of your heart.
Tell wisdom, “You're my sister.” Treat understanding like family.
They'll keep you away from the strange woman, from the outsider who flatters you with her words.
I looked out through the lattice at the window of my house.
I saw a group of inexperienced young people, and one young man stood out for his lack of judgment.
He passed by her corner and headed toward her house,
at twilight as evening fell, then deep into the darkness of night.
A woman came out to meet him, dressed like a prostitute and hiding a scheme.
She's loud and defiant. She never stays home.
She's out in the streets, then in the public squares, lying in wait at every corner.
She grabbed him and kissed him. Without a hint of shame, she said,
“I have meat from my peace offerings. I kept my vows today.
That's why I came out to meet you. I looked hard for you, and here you are.
I've covered my bed with tapestries and striped fabric woven from Egyptian yarn.
I've scented my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
Come, let's get our fill of love till morning. Let's enjoy each other's love.
My husband's away. He's gone on a long trip.
He took a bag of money with him. He won't be home till the full moon.”
Her persuasive words led him astray. Her flattery drew him in.
He followed her right away, like an ox headed for slaughter or a fool stepping into a noose,
until an arrow pierced his liver. He was like a bird rushing into a trap, clueless that it would cost him his life.
So now, sons, listen to me. Pay attention to what I'm saying.
Don't let your heart turn toward her ways. Don't wander down her paths.
She's brought down many people and left them wounded. The ones she's killed could fill an army.
Her house is the road to Sheol, leading down to the rooms of death.
Isn't Wisdom calling out? Can't you hear Understanding raise her voice?
She stands on the heights along the road, right where the paths cross.
By the city gates, right at the entrance, she calls out:
“I'm calling to you, people! I'm raising my voice so everyone can hear.
If you're inexperienced, learn good judgment. If you've been foolish, get some understanding.
Listen. What I have to say is worth hearing, and my words will be right.
I speak the truth. My lips can't stand wickedness.
Everything I say is right. There's nothing twisted or crooked in my words.
They're clear to anyone who understands and right to whoever finds knowledge.
Choose my instruction over silver and knowledge over the finest gold.
Wisdom is worth more than rubies. Nothing you could want comes close.
“I, Wisdom, make my home with good judgment. Learn knowledge and discretion.
To revere the LORD is to hate evil. I hate pride, arrogance, evil ways, and crooked talk.
Good advice and sound knowledge belong to me. I have understanding and power.
Through me kings reign and rulers make just laws.
Through me princes govern, along with nobles and every ruler on earth who rules justly.
I love those who love me. Anyone who really looks for me will find me.
With me are riches and honor, lasting wealth and prosperity.
What I produce beats gold, even pure gold. My yield is worth more than the finest silver.
I walk the road of righteousness, right in the middle of the paths of justice,
so I can give wealth to those who love me and fill their treasuries.
“The LORD possessed me at the start of his work, before the things he did long ago.
I was set in place from everlasting, from the beginning, before the earth existed.
I was born when there were no depths, before there were springs overflowing with water.
Before the mountains were set in place, before the hills, I was born,
when he hadn't made the earth or the fields, or even the first dust of the world.
I was there when he set the heavens in place and drew a circle over the deep,
when he fixed the clouds above and strengthened the springs of the deep,
when he gave the sea its boundary so the waters wouldn't cross his command, and marked out the earth's foundations.
I was there beside him, his craftsman. Day after day I was a delight, always celebrating in front of him,
taking joy in his whole world and delighting in humanity.
“So now, my sons, listen to me. Blessed are those who stay on my paths.
Hear instruction and grow wise. Don't brush it off.
Blessed is anyone who listens to me, watching at my gates day after day, waiting by my doorposts.
Whoever finds me finds life and receives favor from the LORD.
But whoever sins against me harms their own life. Everyone who hates me loves death.”
Wisdom built her house and carved out its seven pillars.
She prepared the meat, mixed the wine, and set the table.
She sent out her servants and called from the highest spots in the city:
“If you're inexperienced, come on in!” To those who lack understanding, she says,
“Come eat my bread and drink the wine I've mixed!
Leave your foolish ways behind and live. Walk the path of understanding.”
Correct a mocker and you'll get insulted. Call out someone wicked and you'll get abuse.
Correct a scoffer and they'll hate you for it. Correct someone wise and they'll love you for it.
Teach wise people and they'll grow wiser. Teach people who do what's right and they'll learn even more.
Reverence for the LORD is where wisdom begins. Knowing the Holy One is understanding.
Through me, you'll have more days and more years of life.
If you're wise, you benefit from your wisdom. If you mock, you carry the consequences yourself.
The woman called Folly is loud and out of control. She has no clue.
She sits by her front door, on a seat high above the city,
calling to people passing by who were walking straight on their way:
“If you're inexperienced, come on in!” To those who lack understanding, she says,
“Stolen water tastes sweet. Food eaten in secret hits different.”
They have no idea the spirits of the dead are there, or that her guests are down in the depths of Sheol.
The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son makes his father glad. A foolish son breaks his mother's heart.
Wealth gained by doing wrong does you no good, but doing what's right saves you from death.
The LORD won't let people who do right go hungry, but he pushes away what the wicked crave.
Lazy hands lead to poverty. Diligent hands build wealth.
A son who gathers in summer is wise. A son who sleeps through harvest brings shame.
Blessings rest on the heads of people who do right, but violence covers the mouths of the wicked.
The memory of people who do right is a blessing. The name of the wicked will rot.
People who are wise at heart accept commands. A fool who won't stop talking will fall.
People who walk with integrity walk securely. People who take crooked paths will get found out.
A sneaky wink causes grief. A fool who won't stop talking will fall.
The words of people who do right are a spring of life, but violence covers the mouths of the wicked.
Hatred starts fights, but love covers every wrong.
People with good judgment speak wisdom. A rod is for the back of the person who lacks understanding.
Wise people store up knowledge. Foolish talk brings ruin close.
A rich person's wealth is their fortified city. Poverty is what brings the poor to ruin.
The work of people who do right leads to life. The gains of the wicked lead to sin.
Listening to correction keeps you on the path of life. Rejecting it leads others astray.
Anyone who hides hatred is lying. Anyone who spreads slander is a fool.
When you talk nonstop, wrongdoing is never far away. It's wise to know when to keep quiet.
The words of people who do right are like the finest silver. The heart of the wicked isn't worth much.
The words of people who do right feed many. Fools die because they lack understanding.
The LORD's blessing brings wealth, and he adds no trouble to it.
Doing wrong is fun to a fool. A person with understanding finds joy in wisdom.
What the wicked dread will catch up with them. People who do right will get what they long for.
When the whirlwind passes, the wicked are gone. People who do right stand firm forever.
Sending a slacker on an errand is like vinegar on your teeth or smoke in your eyes.
Reverence for the LORD adds days to your life. The years of the wicked will be cut short.
People who do right have joy ahead of them. The hopes of the wicked will come to nothing.
The LORD's way is a fortress for people of integrity and ruin for people who do evil.
People who do right will never be uprooted. The wicked won't live in the land.
Wisdom grows from the words of people who do right. The tongue that twists the truth will be cut off.
People who do right know what to say. The wicked twist what's right when they speak.
The LORD hates rigged scales. Honest weights make him glad.
Pride shows up and shame follows. Wisdom comes with humility.
Integrity guides people who live uprightly. Crookedness destroys those who betray others.
Money won't help on the day of wrath, but righteousness rescues from death.
Doing what's right keeps a person of integrity on a straight path. The wicked trip over their own wrongdoing.
The upright are rescued by doing what's right. The unfaithful get trapped by their own evil cravings.
When a wicked person dies, their hope dies too. Everything they expected from their power comes to nothing.
A person who does right gets out of trouble, and the wicked take their place.
The godless ruin their neighbors with their words. Knowledge gets the righteous out of danger.
When things go well for people who do right, the city celebrates. When the wicked perish, people shout for joy.
The blessing of upright people lifts up a city. The words of the wicked tear it down.
Looking down on your neighbor shows a lack of wisdom. Someone with understanding knows when to stay quiet.
A gossip spills what was told in confidence. A trustworthy person keeps a secret.
Without wise guidance a nation falls. With plenty of advisers, there's victory.
Guarantee a stranger's debt and you'll pay for it. Refuse to put yourself up as collateral and you'll be secure.
A gracious woman gains honor. Violent men gain riches.
A merciful person does themselves good. A cruel person brings trouble on their own body.
The wicked earn wages that don't deliver. Sow righteousness and the reward is sure.
Anyone who truly does what's right finds life. Anyone who chases evil finds death.
The LORD detests crooked hearts. People whose ways are blameless make him glad.
Make no mistake, evil won't go unpunished. The children of those who do right will be rescued.
A beautiful woman without good judgment is like a gold ring in a pig's snout.
People who do right desire what's good. The wicked can expect wrath.
One person gives freely and gains even more. Another holds back more than they should and ends up poor.
A generous person will have plenty. Give others water and you'll get water too.
People curse someone who hoards grain, but they bless the person who sells it.
Search hard for what's good and you're seeking favor. Go looking for evil and it'll find you.
Trust your wealth and you'll fall. People who do right will thrive like green leaves. 🌿
Bring trouble on your own household and you'll inherit the wind. A fool will serve someone wise at heart.
What the righteous produce is a tree of life. A wise person wins people over.
Look, even those who do right get repaid here on earth. How much more will the wicked and the sinner?
Anyone who loves correction loves knowledge. Hating correction is foolish.
The LORD shows favor to a good person and condemns whoever plots evil.
Wickedness won't give anyone a firm footing. The roots of people who do right won't be shaken.
A worthy wife is her husband's crown. A wife who brings disgrace is like rot in his bones.
People who do right think about what's fair. The wicked give advice designed to deceive.
The words of the wicked are an ambush for blood. The words of upright people get them out of danger.
The wicked get knocked down and disappear. The household of those who do right will stand.
People earn praise for their wisdom. A twisted mind earns contempt.
It's better to be little known and have a servant than to act important and have no bread.
A person who does right cares about the life of their animal. Even the kindness of the wicked is cruel.
Work your land and you'll have plenty of bread. Chase fantasies and you show how little you understand.
The wicked want the loot of people who do evil. The roots of those who do right keep growing.
Evil people get trapped by their own sinful words. People who do right make it out of trouble.
Good words bring good things to the person who speaks them. The work of your hands brings its own reward.
A fool thinks their way is obviously right. A wise person listens to advice.
A fool lets their irritation show right away. Someone with good judgment lets an insult pass.
A truthful person gives honest testimony. A false witness tells lies.
Careless words can cut like a sword. Wise words can heal.
Truthful words stand forever. A lie lasts only a moment.
People who plot evil carry deceit in their hearts. People who work for peace find joy.
Harm won't come upon those who do right. The wicked will have their fill of trouble.
The LORD hates lying lips. People who live by the truth make him glad.
A person with good judgment keeps what they know to themselves. Fools broadcast the foolishness in their hearts.
Hardworking hands will rule. Laziness ends in forced labor.
Anxiety weighs down the heart. A kind word lifts it up. 💛
People who do right choose their friends carefully. The ways of the wicked lead them astray.
A lazy person won't even roast what they hunted. Hardworking people value what they have.
There's life on the road of righteousness. There's no death on that path.
A wise son listens to his father's instruction. A mocker won't hear a word of correction.
Good words bring good things to the one who speaks them. People who betray others crave violence.
Watch what you say and you'll protect your life. Open your mouth without restraint and you'll come to ruin.
A slacker wants plenty and gets nothing. A diligent person's desires will be fully satisfied.
People who do right hate lies. The wicked bring shame and disgrace.
Doing what's right guards the path of integrity. Wickedness brings the sinner down.
Some people act rich and have nothing. Others act poor and have plenty.
A rich person can pay a ransom for their life. The poor don't get those threats.
The light of people who do right shines brightly. The lamp of the wicked goes out.
Pride only starts fights. Wisdom belongs to people who take advice.
Money gained dishonestly dwindles. Gather it through your own work and it'll grow.
When hope keeps getting put off, the heart grows sick. When longing comes true, it's a tree of life. 🌱
Look down on instruction and you'll pay for it. Respect a command and you'll be rewarded.
The teaching of wise people is a spring of life. It turns you away from deadly traps.
Good understanding wins favor. The road of the unfaithful is hard.
A person with good judgment acts on what they know. A fool puts their foolishness on display.
A wicked messenger gets into trouble. A trusted envoy brings healing.
Reject discipline and you'll end up poor and ashamed. Listen to correction and you'll be honored.
Getting what you longed for feels sweet to the soul. Fools can't stand turning away from evil.
Walk with wise people and you'll grow wise. Keep company with fools and you'll get hurt.
Trouble chases sinners. Good things reward people who do right.
A good person leaves an inheritance for their grandchildren. A sinner's wealth is stored up for people who do right.
The fields of the poor can grow plenty of food. Injustice sweeps it all away.
A parent who spares the rod hates their son. A parent who loves him takes care to discipline him.
A person who does right eats until they're satisfied. The wicked go hungry.
A wise woman builds up her household. A foolish one tears hers down with her own hands.
Someone who walks uprightly reveres the LORD. Someone whose ways are crooked despises him.
A fool's talk earns them a beating. Wise people's words protect them.
Without oxen the feeding trough stays clean, but an ox's strength brings a big harvest.
An honest witness won't lie. A false witness pours out lies.
A mocker looks for wisdom and comes up empty. Knowledge comes easily to someone with good judgment.
Stay away from a fool. You won't hear anything worth learning from their lips.
Wise people think about where they're headed. Fools get caught up in deceit.
Fools make fun of making amends for sin. People who live uprightly show goodwill.
The heart knows its own hurt and joy. A stranger can't fully share either.
The house of the wicked will come down. Even the tent of the upright will thrive.
A road can look right to you and still end in death.
You can laugh and still have a heavy heart. Even good times can end in grief.
Unfaithful people will get paid back for their ways. Good people will get the reward of theirs.
An inexperienced person believes everything. Someone with good judgment watches where they step.
A wise person takes evil seriously and stays clear of it. A fool gets heated and rushes in.
People with quick tempers do foolish things. People who scheme are hated.
People without experience inherit foolishness. Those with good judgment wear knowledge like a crown.
Evil people bow before good people, and the wicked bow at the gates of those who do right.
Even their neighbors avoid someone who's poor. A rich person has plenty of friends.
Looking down on your neighbor is a sin. Blessed is anyone who shows kindness to the poor.
People who plot evil lose their way. Faithful love and truth belong to those who plan good.
Hard work pays off. Just talking about it leads to poverty.
Wealth is a crown for the wise. Fools wear their foolishness like a crown.
An honest witness saves lives. A false witness deals in lies.
Reverence for the LORD is a strong fortress, and he'll be a shelter for his children.
Reverence for the LORD is a fountain of life. It turns people away from deadly traps.
A king's glory comes from having many people. Without people, a ruler falls.
Being slow to anger shows deep understanding. A short fuse puts foolishness on display.
A peaceful heart gives life to the body. Envy eats away at the bones.
Oppressing the poor insults their Maker. Showing kindness to someone in need honors him.
The wicked fall when disaster hits. People who do right have a refuge even in death.
Wisdom rests in an understanding heart. It makes itself known even in the hearts of fools.
Doing what's right lifts up a nation. Sin disgraces any people.

You'll have plenty of goat's milk for yourself, your household, and the young women who serve you.
The wicked run when nobody's chasing them. People who do right are bold as lions.
When a land rebels, rulers come and go. Someone with understanding and knowledge keeps things steady.
A poor person who oppresses other poor people is like driving rain that wipes out the crops.
People who abandon the law hype up the wicked. People who keep the law stand against them.
People who do evil don't get justice. Those who seek the LORD understand it fully.
It's better to be poor and walk with integrity than to be rich and take crooked paths.
A son who keeps the law is wise. A son who hangs around with gluttons shames his father.
Anyone who gets rich by charging excessive interest piles up money for someone who'll show mercy to the poor.
Turn a deaf ear to the law, and even your prayer is detestable.
Lead upright people down an evil path and you'll fall into your own trap. People who live with integrity will inherit good things.
A rich person may think they're wise, but a poor person with understanding sees right through them.
When people who do right win, there's great celebration. When the wicked rise, people go into hiding.
Hide your sins and you won't prosper. Own up to them and turn away from them, and you'll find mercy.
Blessed is anyone who stays reverent. Harden your heart and you'll fall into trouble.
A wicked ruler over helpless people is like a roaring lion or a charging bear.
A tyrant has no judgment. A ruler who hates dishonest gain will have a long life.
Someone tormented by guilt for bloodshed will be on the run till death. Nobody will support them.
Walk with integrity and you'll be kept safe. Take crooked paths and you'll fall without warning.
Work your land and you'll have plenty of food. Chase fantasies and you'll get your fill of poverty.
A faithful person is rich in blessings. Someone in a rush to get rich won't go unpunished.
Playing favorites is wrong, yet someone will do wrong for a piece of bread.
A stingy person rushes after riches and has no idea poverty is waiting for them.
In the end, honest correction earns more favor than smooth talk.
Rob your father or mother and say, “There's nothing wrong with that,” and you're in league with someone who destroys.
Greed stirs up fights. Trust the LORD and you'll prosper.
Anyone who trusts only themselves is a fool. Walk in wisdom and you'll be kept safe.
Give to the poor and you won't go without. Close your eyes to them and many curses will come your way.
When the wicked rise, people hide. When the wicked perish, those who do right thrive.
Keep digging in your heels every time someone corrects you, and ruin will hit without warning. There'll be no fixing it.
When people who do right thrive, everyone celebrates. When the wicked rule, people groan.
Anyone who loves wisdom brings their father joy. Anyone who keeps company with prostitutes blows through their wealth.
A king who rules with justice keeps the land steady. A king who takes bribes tears it down.
Flattering your neighbor is like spreading a net under their feet.
Evil people are trapped by their own sin. People who do right can sing for joy.
People who do right care about justice for the poor. The wicked don't care to understand it.
Mockers get a whole city worked up. Wise people calm its anger.
When a wise person takes a fool to court, the fool rages or mocks. Either way, there's no peace.
People out for blood hate anyone with integrity. They seek the lives of those who live uprightly.
A fool lets all their anger out. A wise person keeps it under control.
If a ruler listens to lies, all their officials turn wicked.
Poor people and their oppressors have this in common: the LORD gives both of them sight.
A king who judges the poor fairly will have a throne that stands forever.
The rod of correction teaches wisdom. A child left to do whatever they want brings shame to their mother.
When the wicked multiply, sin multiplies. People who do right will see them fall.
Correct your son and he'll bring you peace. He'll bring joy to your soul.
Without revelation, people throw off restraint. Blessed is anyone who keeps the law.
Words alone won't correct a servant. They may understand and still refuse to respond.
See someone who speaks before they think? There's more hope for a fool than for them.
Pamper a servant from childhood and in the end they'll become like a son.
An angry person starts fights. Someone full of rage commits sin after sin.
Pride brings people low. A humble spirit earns honor.
Anyone who partners with a thief acts against their own life. They hear the oath but don't dare testify.
Fear of other people is a trap. Trust the LORD and you'll be kept safe.
Many people want a ruler's favor, but justice comes from the LORD.
Dishonest people detest those who do right. People who walk uprightly detest the wicked.
These are the words of Agur son of Jakeh, a revelation. He speaks to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:
“Surely I'm more ignorant than anyone. I don't even have ordinary human understanding.
I haven't learned wisdom, and I don't have knowledge of the Holy One.

Who's gone up to heaven and come down? Who's gathered the wind in their fists or wrapped the waters in their clothes? Who set the farthest ends of the earth in place? What's his name, and what's his son's name, if you know?
“Every word God speaks is flawless. He's a shield to those who take shelter in him.
Don't add to his words, or he'll correct you and you'll be exposed as a liar.
“I've asked you for two things. Don't deny them to me before I die.
Keep falsehood and lies far away from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches. Feed me with just the food I need.
If I have too much, I might deny you and say, ‘Who's the LORD?’ If I'm poor, I might steal and dishonor my God's name.
“Don't slander a servant to their master, or they'll curse you and you'll be held guilty.
There's a generation that curses their fathers and won't bless their mothers.
There's a generation that thinks it's pure even though its filth hasn't been washed away.
There's a generation with eyes lifted high. You can see their pride in the way they look at you.
There's a generation with teeth like swords and jaws like knives, ready to devour the poor off the earth and the needy from among humanity.
“The leech has two daughters who keep saying, ‘Give! Give!’ Three things never get enough. Four never say, ‘That's enough!’
Sheol, a womb that can't bear children, ground that never gets enough water, and fire that never says, ‘Enough!’
“The eye that mocks its father and scorns obeying its mother will be picked out by ravens in the valley and eaten by young eagles.
“Three things are too amazing for me. Four I just don't understand:
how an eagle moves through the air, how a snake moves over a rock, how a ship moves through the open sea, and the way of a man with a young woman.
“Here's how an adulterous woman acts: she eats, wipes her mouth, and says, ‘I did nothing wrong.’
“Three things make the earth shake. Four are more than it can bear:
a servant who becomes king, a fool with a full stomach,
an unloved woman who gets married, and a servant who inherits her mistress's place.
“Four things on earth are small and incredibly wise:
ants aren't strong, yet they store up food in summer.
Hyraxes are weak, yet they build their homes in the rocks.
Locusts have no king, yet they march in ranks.
You can catch a lizard with your hands, yet there it is in kings' palaces.
“Three things walk with dignity. Four move with a stately stride:
the lion, strongest of the animals, who backs down for none;
the greyhound, the male goat, and the king nobody can rise up against.
“If you've foolishly hyped yourself up or thought about doing evil, put your hand over your mouth.
Churning milk brings out butter, twisting a nose brings out blood, and stirring up anger brings out a fight.”
These are the words of King Lemuel, the revelation his mother taught him:
“Oh, my son! The son I carried, the son of my vows!
Don't give your strength away to women or follow the ways that ruin kings.
Lemuel, kings have no business drinking wine. Rulers have no business asking where the strong drink is.
They might drink and forget the law, twisting the justice that people in trouble are owed.
Give strong drink to someone who's about to die, and wine to someone bitter in soul.
Let them drink and forget their poverty, and let their misery slip from their mind.
Speak up for those who can't speak, and take up the cause of everyone left helpless.
Speak up and judge fairly. Get justice for the poor and needy.”
Who can find a worthy woman? She's worth far more than rubies.
Her husband trusts her with his whole heart, and he'll have no shortage of gain.
She does him good and never harms him, all the days of her life.
She looks for wool and flax and gets to work gladly with her hands.
She's like a fleet of merchant ships, bringing her food from far away.
She gets up while it's still dark, feeds her household, and sets out portions for the young women who serve her.
She sizes up a field and buys it. From what her own hands earn, she plants a vineyard.
She gets herself ready with strength and makes her arms strong.
She sees that her business is making a profit. Her lamp stays lit at night.
She reaches for the distaff and takes the spindle in her hands.
She opens her arms to the poor and reaches out to people in need.
She doesn't fear snow for her household. Everyone in the house is dressed in scarlet.
She makes her own coverings. She dresses in fine linen and purple.
Her husband is respected at the city gates, where he sits with the elders of the land.
She makes linen clothes and sells them. She supplies sashes to the merchant.
She wears strength and dignity like clothes. She can laugh at what's ahead.
When she speaks, wisdom comes out. She teaches with kindness.
She watches over how her household is doing. She doesn't eat the bread of idleness.
Her children stand up and call her blessed. Her husband praises her too:
“Many women do noble things, but you rise above them all.”
Charm can fool you, and beauty doesn't last. A woman who reveres the LORD deserves praise.
Give her what her work has earned. Let what she's done bring her praise at the city gates!
